key_insight: The paper proves that a standard mesh-free peridynamic discretization with bond breakage converges for fixed horizon, even with irreversible damage and one-point quadrature included in the analysis.
engineering_relevance: This gives fracture-modeling practitioners a theoretical guarantee that a widely used nonlocal simulation scheme can reliably approximate the intended peridynamic dynamics at a chosen length scale.
method: Analyze a dynamic nonlinear bond-based peridynamic model with a mathematically well-posed damage regularization.
Include the mesh-free discretization and its one-point quadrature directly in the convergence proof.
Derive local Lipschitz bounds for the continuous displacement solution under locally L-Lipschitz input data.
evidence_signal: The evaluation is analytical rather than numerical: convergence is established in the natural norm C^1([0,T], L^∞(Ω)^d), and the spatial regularity result supports the proof.
watch_item: The result is only for fixed horizon δ > 0 and does not address the important limit as δ approaches 0, so it does not yet recover a sharp classical fracture limit.
paper_title: On the Convergence of the Mesh-Free Discretization of a Non-Linear Bond-Based Peridynamic Model with a Bond-Breakage Criterion
